prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows the camera wearer standing right against a stone service counter (bright on the right, ~0.3–0.6 m away) that recedes diagonally toward the upper left (~1.5–2.5 m away). In frames 1 and 5, the camera wearer's own hands, wallet, and payment terminal in the lower foreground are bright (~0.3–0.5 m, within immediate grasp), while in frames 2–5 a sanitizer pump bottle sits on the window ledge ~0.6–0.9 m to the upper right (within arm's reach) and a second person (a worker behind the counter) appears in the lower left of frames 2–5 at ~1.2–1.8 m away (~1.0–1.2 m left of and below the bottle, out of the camera wearer's reach). Across the 5 frames, the camera pitches up and turns slightly left from frame 1 (looking down at the hands and floor) to frames 2–4 (looking across the counter ledge and menu board), then pitches back down and right in frame 5 as the right hand holds the terminal up toward the counter window. The depth map makes the continuous 3D receding plane of the stone wall, the step of the window ledge, and the exact contour of the thin power cord in frame 1 much clearer than in the textured RGB image. However, it is unreliable around the transparent plexiglass sneeze guard (which it completely looks through instead of registering as a near surface) and in frame 1 where the tilted stone wall at the top is rendered overly bright compared to the foreground hands.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities across the sequence: the camera wearer's hands and arms (`person`, lower foreground, ~0.3–0.5 m away) holding a wallet and payment terminal (mislabelled as `cell phone`) in frames 1 and 5, the pump bottle (`bottle`, middle-right on the ledge, ~0.6–0.9 m away) in frames 3 and 4, and the counter worker's torso and blue-gloved left arm (`person`, lower left behind the counter, ~1.2–1.8 m away and ~1.0 m left of the bottle) in frames 3 and 4. In frame 1 the camera wearer's left hand partially occludes the wallet while the right hand holds the terminal below it, and in frames 2–5 the worker is heavily occluded by the lower-left frame border and counter equipment, with their head out of view and their torso facing right/upward toward the counter register within their own arm's reach. As the camera shifts from looking down at the held devices (frame 1) to the counter window (frames 2–4) and back down to the raised terminal (frame 5), segmentation tracks the entry and exit of these objects in the field of view. It helps separate the motion-blurred right hand and terminal in frame 1 and the dark-shadowed worker in the lower left of frames 3–4 from the busy background more clearly than RGB alone. However, the map is unreliable in frame 2 (missing all objects entirely), frame 5 (missing the bottle and worker while double-labelling the wallet and terminal as `cell phone` and splitting the hand into separate `person` masks), and throughout the strip where static structural elements like the counter, plexiglass barrier, and register are unsegmented.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's left hand in the lower-left foreground of frame 1 (~0.3–0.4 m from the camera), showing the thumb and fingers curled around the left edge of the wallet within immediate reach. It provides no skeletons for the camera wearer's right hand in frames 1 and 5, nor for the counter worker visible in the lower-left background (~1.2–1.8 m away, facing right toward the register with their head out of frame) in frames 2–5. Consequently, across the 5 frames, the pose map only captures the initial presence of the left hand before it moves out of the lower frame boundary as the camera tilts upward in frames 2–4 and stays out of view in frame 5. In frame 1, the 2D joint keypoints clearly resolve the exact finger articulation and pinch grip of the gloved left hand despite the wallet occluding the palm and fingertips. However, the map is highly unreliable across the rest of the sequence, failing to detect the motion-blurred gloved right hand in frame 1, the partially occluded right hand holding the terminal in frame 5, and the worker's torso and blue-gloved hand in frames 2–5.
